name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield slipped below 5.2% on 23 Nov from above 5.35% on 16 Nov; long yields still near multi-decade highs
state: The 10-year gilt yield rose above 5.35% on 16 Nov, its highest since 23 Oct, as markets priced a further Bank of England rise in December, then fell to about 5.23% on 20 Nov and below 5.2% on 23 Nov (Trading Economics). The Bank raised rates on 5 Nov and warned inflation would approach 5% (CNBC). The 10-year's monthly move is inside the 40bp line; Watch is kept because the 30-year yield, near 5.72% on 20 Nov, remains close to levels last seen in 1998, with no weak auction or BoE intervention found.
for_you: Higher gilt yields feed through to fixed mortgage pricing, annuity rates and government borrowing costs. Households remortgaging in the coming months are most exposed to these conditions.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt near multi-decade highs (~5.72%, 20 Nov); 10y monthly move under 40bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — UK gilt yields news stream (16–23 Nov)
CNBC — Bank of England hikes interest rate, warns inflation will near 5%

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
